source_text: (Sed Christus diuortium inhibet dicens: qui dimiserit uxorem suam et aliam duxerit, adulterium committet, (et) qui dimissam a uiro duxerit, aeque adulter est, - ut sic quoque prohibeat diuortium, inlicitum facit repudiatae matrimonium — Moyses uero permittit repudium in Deuteronomio: si sumserit quis uxorem et habitauerit cum ea, et euenerit non inuenire eam apud eum gratiam, eo quod inuentum sit in illa impudicum negotium, scribet libellum repudii et dabit in manu eius et dimittet illam de domo sua.
pass_a_gloss: But Christ forbids divorce, saying: he who dismisses his wife and leads another, commits adultery, and he who leads her who has been dismissed by her husband, is equally an adulterer, - so that He also prohibits divorce, makes the marriage of her who has been repudiated unlawful - but indeed Moses permits repudiation in Deuteronomy: if someone takes a wife and dwells with her, and it happens that he does not find her with favor before him, because an impudent deed is found in her, he will write a bill of divorce and give it into her hand and dismiss her from his house.

choices.why: accurate translation of the Latin verb
preserves the comparative sense of the Latin

pass_b_english: Christ forbids divorce. He says that a man who dismisses his wife and marries another commits adultery, and a man who marries a woman dismissed by her husband is equally an adulterer. By making the marriage of a repudiated woman unlawful, he thereby also prohibits divorce. Moses, however, permits repudiation in Deuteronomy: if a man takes a wife, lives with her, and then finds no favor in her because he has discovered an indecent deed in her, he must write a bill of divorce, hand it to her, and send her from his house (Deuteronomy).

anf_compare.notes: Drafted from source only; ANF not shown to drafter.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass A preserves the clause structure and the specific nuances of 'aeque adulter est' and 'inlicitum facit'. Pass B provides a fluent rendering that maintains the meaning and correctly identifies the scripture reference (Deuteronomy) as an allusion/quotation within the text.
